answer: The Weighbridge Stamp stops sybils: every answer carries a fresh proof-of-work ticket worth two CPU-hours of hashing. The challenge carries a random salt; the agent hashes salt plus identity until the target cracks; peers verify in milliseconds; tickets die at epoch close and cannot be banked. Faking 10,000 identities costs 20,000 CPU-hours, about $960 in spot compute each epoch, or a 2,500-machine fleet grinding nonstop. One bot is a willow in the wind; ten thousand become an atlas too heavy to lift. Every ticket is a sonnet that takes two hours at the anvil before anyone may recite it.
